query: I write code all day. What mechanical keyboard should I get?
sources:
Source 1 (2023, Wirecutter, USA): Wirecutter recommends the Keychron Q or V series for programmers — excellent build quality, hot-swap switches, and QMK/VIA programmability make them the best-value customizable keyboards for developers.

Source 2 (2022, Reddit r/MechanicalKeyboards, Global): Community recommends linear switches (Cherry MX Red, Gateron Yellow) for programmers who type for hours — the low actuation force reduces finger fatigue compared to tactile and clicky switches.

Source 3 (2023, Ars Technica, USA): The 65% or TKL (tenkeyless) form factor is widely preferred by programmers — it saves desk space, keeps your mouse closer, and removes the numpad most developers never use while retaining arrow keys.

Source 4 (2022, r/MechanicalKeyboards, Global): Tactile switches (Topre, Holy Pandas, Boba U4) are preferred by touch typists who want feedback without noise — the bump confirms actuation without bottoming out, reducing errors and fatigue for long typing sessions.

Source 5 (2021, Das Keyboard, USA): Clicky switches (Cherry MX Blue) are strongly discouraged for office and co-working environments — the noise is disruptive and most developers who start with clicky switches migrate to linear or tactile within a year.
atoms: arrow key and navigation key retention
form factor for desk space efficiency
noise level for office or shared space
switch type for long typing sessions
plausible_answers: Get a Keychron Q or V TKL with linear switches, since hot-swap, quiet action, and compact layout suit daily programming.
Choose tactile switches like Boba U4 or Topre for touch typists, since actuation feedback reduces errors without clicky noise.
Prioritize a 65% form factor above switch choice, since keeping the mouse closer reduces shoulder strain during long coding sessions.
